scope: Standalone research framing, nontriviality, distinctness, sufficient raw inputs, necessary background, answer leakage, and solver-contract consistency. Numerical execution and verifier correctness are separate reviews.

questions.title: Which representation gives more reliable phase identification on held-out simulated patterns?
How does increasing phase count affect recovery of constituent identities from XRD and virtual-PDF template fits?
How do additive noise and smooth background alter virtual PDFs across distance windows?
How well do simulation-derived references recover secondary phases in measured binary mixtures as abundance decreases?

findings.issue: split_trace schema initially implied every recorded single-phase test ID is evaluated by Q2/Q4.
findings.resolution: Schema now identifies complete reference partition and directs evaluated mixture IDs to predictions.csv.

findings.issue: README initially omitted explicitly referenced protocol sections from applicable definitions.
findings.resolution: README now includes referenced section definitions and states that no other question result is needed.

limitations: Labels remain supplied separately for scientific evaluation; anonymized names do not by themselves enforce label-blind inference.
Controlled baseline references do not reproduce historical CNN results.
Q2 phase-count groups differ in constituent composition; interpretation is descriptive.
Q3 energy retention does not establish retained classification accuracy.
Q4 candidate formulas and binary cardinality are known; intensity coefficients are not mass fractions.
